Testimony of Senator Brad Farrin
LD 182, "An Act to Require the Department of Health and Human Services to Establish MaineCare Reimbursement Rates for the Maine Veterans' Homes on a Per Resident Basis"
Before the Health and Human Services Committee April 1, 2025

Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services: I am Brad Farrin and I have the honor of representing the people of Senate District 3, which includes towns in Kennebec, Somerset and Penobscot counties. I am before you today testify in support of LD 182, "An Act to Require the Department of Health and Human Services to Establish MaineCare Reimbursement Rates for the Maine Veterans' Homes on a Per Resident Basis."
As this committee knows well, and as the BerryDunn report from the Stakeholders Group makes clear, Maine Veterans' Homes (MVH) have an immediate and on-going need for additional funding. We heard from MVH's CEO that MVH faces an estimated $15.5 million yearly gap between its costs and its reimbursements. While MVH is able to reduce this gap to $10.3 million by accessing federal VA funding, it still leaves the Homes in the red, year after year.
During the debate around L.D. 2001 from the 130th legislature, we heard about the compassionate and high-level care MVH provides across its six locations. We also heard that the Homes need additional funding to maintain operations and continue this level of care.
This bill would provide that long-term, sustainable funding. By adjusting its reimbursement rules, the state would provide additional funds which would be matched in federal funds, ultimately closing this yearly multi million dollar gap between reimbursement rates and costs to deliver that care.
By supporting this bill, I wanted to make sure we had the vehicle necessary to adequately fund the Homes in the future. The important point is that we--the Legislature--need and must adequately fund them. To underscore this point, let me read the statement of policy in L.D. 2001, now included as 37-B �601(1).
It is the policy of the State to ensure the provision of long-term care, support and services to eligible veterans and their family members in every region of the State and the intent of the Legislature that the Maine Veterans' Homes implement this policy by providing long-term care, support and related services to fulfill the State's moral obligation to promote the well-being and dignity of the veterans who have served their nation, often in times of war and at great cost.

MVH's culture is unique and unmatched, as shown by:

In summary of my first 90 days evaluation: MVH is a system deserving of continuous and

LDl82 addresses the discrepancy between the cost of providing nationally recognized care and the reimbursement received. Residents with MaineCare account for over 50% of our funding source. While other nursing homes operate within the MaineCare reimbursement, We incur $3.0 million
in additional and quantifiable costs not faced by other facilities. This is due to higher staffing ratios,
lower reimbursement rates for 70% service-disabled veterans, physical plant requirements, and
contributions to MainePERS instead of Social Security. Additionally, there are unquantifiable
expenses related to compliance with VA regulations, such as occupancy requirements and
mandated eligibility criteria that cannot be quantified.
Maine Veterans' Homes faces unique restrictions compared to others in the long-term care industry. When the Board of Trustees decided to close two homes (one in Machias, the other in Caribou), LD200l was passed requiring a Stakeholders Group, chaired by the then Commissioner

10041268:
Testimony in support of LD 182 Cynthia Grant Addison, Maine
My name is Cynthia Grant and I am a resident of Addison, Washington County. Today, I wish to express my strong support for LD 182.
This legislation is essential to maintaining the skilled staffing, specialized programs, and services that are tailored to the unique needs of the residents at our Maine Veterans' Homes. LD 182 would create a more accurate and fair reimbursement system by basing per resident payment rates on the actual care and service needs of the residents.
I speak to you today as the daughter of a WWII veteran and the current caregiver advocate for my mother, Julia Worcester, who resides at the Maine Veterans' Home in Machias.
My father was a proud to be a veteran, a long-time laborer, and a man whose family never required public assistance. When my mother was 49, after having worked more than 20 years in multiple factories and restaurants, and long before "non-traditional" students were common, went to college to become a teacher, believing that between their combined Social Security, savings, and her teacher's retirement, they could remain self-sufficient to their final hours.
Unfortunately, her efforts were undercut by the Windfall Elimination Provision. In 2003, when she 73 years old, she flew to Washington, D.C. to testify for its repeal at the request of Senator Susan Collins. Even though the provision was recently repealed, it's too late for my mother's benefit.
Today, at 94, she lives with dementia and is blinded by macular degeneration. Because her husband served his country, she resides at Maine Veterans' Home in Machias. The specialized care she receives is a direct result of his sacrifice. If he were alive, he would be overwhelmed with gratefulness and relieved that his service secured this support for her.
Despite her careful planning, she has outlived her finances, and her care is now partially covered by MaineCare. Not because she lived irresponsibly, but because none of us know how long we will live or how costly our care will be in the final years of our lives.
Dementia and blindness are cruel diagnoses, but my mother receives excellent and compassionate care. These facilities and their staff deserve to be well-supported and to have the resources they need to continue providing this level of service.
LD 182 is about ensuring that our Veterans' Homes can sustain quality care and attract and retain skilled staff. This is about doing right by those who did everything they could to provide for themselves, and for us.
My parents, and many others, did their due diligence. It is our turn. I urge you to support LD 182 and ensure that MaineCare reimbursement truly reflects the cost of care at Maine Veterans' Homes.
Thank you for consideration of my plea and for your service to the people of Maine.
10041297:
Written Statement For
LD 182 - "An Act to Require the Department of Health and Human Services to Establish MaineCare Reimbursement Rates for the Maine Veterans' Homes on a Per Resident Basis"
April 1, 2025 Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and other distinguished members of the Health and Human Services Committee; my name is Don Lagace, and I wish to submit my written statement in support of L.D. 182, " An Act to Require the Department of Health and Human Services to Establish MaineCare Reimbursement Rates for the Maine Veterans' Homes on a Per Resident Basis"
I am the Chair of the Maine Veterans' Homes (MVH) Board of Trustees. I retired in December 2020 as a Brigadier General after almost 39 years of military service in the Maine Army National Guard. I am honored and privileged to serve on the MVH Board with an incredible group of veterans and business community leaders.
Sustainable funding with LD 182 at $6.8MM of state funds when combined with $424K in Special Revenue Fund and matched with $6.3MM in federal funds closes a financial MaineCare gap that is critical in keeping MVH's system of care viable in the state of Maine.
Currently, MaineCare reimbursement does not fully cover the real costs of caring for each resident. LD 182 would change this by setting per-resident payment rates based on actual care and service needs.
The following brief history will help to establish a better picture of MVH's posture. After years of operational funding challenges and unsuccessful attempts in securing

funding from the State of Maine, the Maine Veterans' Homes Board of Trustees voted to close the Caribou and Machias facilities late in 2021. The Governor and 130th Legislature's 2022 session responded with a financial commitment by introducing LD 2001. The Board of Trustees agreed to work with the Governor and Legislature and changed direction by voting to maintain all six homes with the commitment from the State of Maine. LD 2001 also directed the Maine Veterans' Homes, in collaboration with the Commissioner of Defense, Veterans, and Emergency Management and the Commissioner of Health and Human Services, to convene a group of relevant stakeholders beginning in August, 2022 to develop a plan for the long-term viability and continuous operation of the Maine Veterans' Homes locations designated in the Maine Revised Statutes, Title 37-B, section 601. The stakeholder group was directed to seek input from veterans and their families, employees of the Maine Veterans' Homes and people in the communities served by the Maine Veterans' Homes. I represented the MVH Board of Trustees as Chair of the Stakeholders Group along with Co-Chairs, DHHS Commissioner Jeanne Lambrew, and DVEM Commissioner, Major General Doug Farnham.
The Stakeholders Group included representatives from the Governor's Office, VA Togus, Veterans Services Offices, Maine Veterans Coordinating Committee, Long Term Care Ombudsman, Maine Health Care Association, MVH Employees, Residents, and Family Members. Maine Veterans' Homes (MVH) and Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) engaged BerryDunn as a consultant given their depth of expertise in the senior living industry. Their scope of work included a comparative study of State Veterans' Homes' (SVHs) payment systems, preparing and presenting Maine veteran demand projections for skilled, long-term care and assisted living services, a workforce analysis, conducting focus groups, and analyzing findings. I presented the following Stakeholder Group findings and recommendations to the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee on 1 March 2023.

Stakeholder's Group Recommendations
Purpose: In an effort to continue and enhance our focus on veterans in Maine Veterans' Homes and across the state, we (the Maine Veterans' Homes Stakeholders Group) created the following list of shared principles/recommendations that makes financial sense for the sustainability of the organization and meets a `do no harm' financial criteria:
� Keep the current non-profit model versus a state-owned or operated Veterans' Homes - BerryDunn's comparative study of ten State Veterans' Homes (SVHs), demographic demand projection, workforce analysis, and focus group sessions depicted nationwide challenges facing MVH and other SVHs; however, MVH's unique non-profit model was determined to be preferable (greater quality and significantly less costly than the US average for SVHs - approximately $300 less per resident per day).
� Suggest that the legislature examine financing options used in other states, as described in the report to ensure MVH financial sustainability - After working with the Stakeholder Group for six months, it became clear that financial sustainability for MVH was vital to its continued existence.
� Maintain quality of care - Four nursing homes in the MVH system have a 5-star rating from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). Only 10% of nursing homes nationally achieve a 5-star rating. Maine Veterans' Homes also recently received the Pinnacle Customer Experience Award in all six locations for being in the top 15% of nursing homes nationally. Three MVH facilities have achieved elite status as National Gold Award recipients for sustained excellence in quality by the American Health Care Association - MVHs are the only SVHs and among just 51 facilities across the country to earn the award in more than 25 years since the program's inception! Quality will continue to remain at the forefront for MVH veterans.

� Remain open in current geographic locations - Adopted by the Stakeholder Group and fully supported by MVH Board of Trustees, we recognize MVH's statewide reach, but this six-home footprint needs to be adequately funded to ensure financial sustainability.
� Diversify services to support a continuum of care for Veterans - MVH continues to explore outpatient therapies and expand its pharmacy services and similar opportunities to further serve veterans and their families.
� Develop shared staff relationship and recruitment strategies to address workforce challenges - MVH has since all but eliminated Agency staffing and has stabilized and enhanced its direct care labor pool.
Immediately following the Stakeholders Group's recommendation for sustainable funding for MVH the 131st Legislature passed one-year funding of $8.6MM for MVH in July 2023 with LD 985 in addition to $2.4 million that was included in the Governor's biennial budget. However, to date, MVH has not received all those funds. In 2024, MVH received $4.8 million of the appropriated funds. In January 2025, we received an additional $2.1 million but this still leaves MVH $2.2MM short of the funds appropriated based on the approved MaineCare shortfall.
The 131st Legislature's Second Session also passed one-year funding of $13.3MM (General Fund, Matching Federal Funds, and Special Revenue Funds combined) for MVH in April 2024 with LD 2214 but to date MVH has not received any of the appropriated funds.
No one is more committed to, vested in, or capable of serving Maine's veterans than the MVH Board and the dedicated leaders and employees of the organization. Since the Board's commitment to keeping all six MVH homes open in 2022, MVH leadership has developed and implemented a roadmap of cost optimization levers including stabilized staffing, increased revenue and census, and numerous other cost reduction initiatives. MVH leadership and the Board continues to assess operational

challenges and opportunities to maintain its commitment to Maine's Veterans and their families.
Two years after the Stakeholders Group's recommendation for the Legislature to provide sustainable funding to MVH, the HHS Committee is postured to fulfill the recommendation and meet Maine's moral obligation to our Veterans.
Once passed, LD 182 will preserve a system of care that honors the commitment made to those who offered everything to protect our freedom through their service to this country. It's a small price to pay to honor our Veterans and enable MVH to continue its legacy as one of the premier long-term care systems in the Nation for quality, innovation, and service. Maine's Veterans deserve nothing less!
We truly appreciate the support from Representative Supica, Senator Hickman, and many others from this Committee and Maine's Legislature.
Thank you for the opportunity to submit my testimony.
DONALD O. LAGACE JR. Brigadier General, USA Retired Chairperson, MVH Board of Trustees

Good afternoon, Sen. Ingwersen, Rep. Meyer and esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee. I am Representative Marshall Archer from House District 129, which includes part of Saco. I am a proud member of the l32nd Legislature's Veterans Caucus, the current commander of a local
veterans' service organization and a former aide-de-camp to a national commander of a well-known
veterans' organization that advocated for those who served in war zones. I am also the son of a Vietnam veteran who resides in a Maine Veterans' Home. I stand before you today in strong support of this
crucial bill that will directly impact the care our veterans receive in Maine.
This legislation requires the Department of Health and Human Services to establish reimbursement rates for Maine Veterans' Homes services covered by the MaineCare program. Our veterans deserve world-
class care, yet due to the complexity of federal regulations and rising costs, these essential services face financial strain.
Newer Maine Veterans' Homes operate under a unique model required by the VA featuring smaller, 10-
to-16-room units designed to foster a home-like environment with a full ecosystem of care. Unlike
standard MaineCare facilities, these homes maintain higher staffing levels to meet the complex medical
needs of veterans, many of whom face multiple health conditions and higher acuity levels.
Additionally, they must comply with a distinct set of bureaucratic regulatory demands from the Department of Veterans Affairs that do not apply to traditional MaineCare recipients or providers. These federal mandates, while ensuring high quality care, significantly increase operational costs. Yet these federal mandates are not currently reflected in MaineCare's reimbursement structure.
The Veterans Caucus recently met with Director Klawitter of Maine Veterans' Homes, who underscored
these challenges. Without adequate reimbursement, these facilities struggle to sustain the level of care our veterans need and deserve.

securing the care they have earned.

Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Health and Human Services,
Thank you for the opportunity to provide information in opposition of 182, An Act to Require the Department ofHealth and Human Services to Establish MaineCare Reimbursement Rates for the Maine Veterans' Homes on a Per Resident Basis.
This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services to establish reimbursement rates for Maine Veterans' Homes services covered by the MaineCare program using a facility-specific,
per diem methodology calculation. Specifically, the bill requires the MaineCare program to reimburse veterans' facilities for covered services on a per resident daily rate basis that will reimburse the portion of the total MaineCare allowable cost of operating each veterans` facility
attributable to the provision of services to residents who receive MaineCare benefits. It requires
the Department to index the rates to inflation annually and authorizes the department to contract with a 3rd party to derive or review the rates.
This bill perpetuates a system of rate setting which conflicts with 22 M.R.S. � 3 17 3 -J by establishing reimbursement methodology that has not been developed through the statutory, systematic, methodological approach.
MaineCare recently completed a long process of nursing facility rate reform. The Department did not receive any public comments during this rate determination for nursing facilities that
indicated that Maine Veterans' Home facilities should receive different rates from all other
facilities; however, this bill calls for the development of rates specific to individual Maine
Veterans' Home facilities. This runs contrary to our general rate reform process and principles
established under 22 M.R.S. � 3173-J, including that reimbursement should be consistent and equitable across providers of the same services.
Should this bill move forward, rate determination process requirements set forth in 22 M.R.S.
�3 173-J will need to be observed. The Department would be required to request the necessary
state plan amendments from the federal Department of Health and Human Services, Centers for

Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and adopt routine technical rules upon federal
approval. Maine Veterans' Homes would observe a different reimbursement methodology from
other nursing facilities and, as a result, reimbursement amounts would differ from the newly
implemented methodology. This change would move MaineCare back toward an inequitable
system of reimbursements, one that the Department and Legislature has worked hard to address in the last several years. Additionally, system configuration changes would be required to operationalize the bill's proposed reimbursement methodology for Maine Veterans' Homes.
Above and beyond what other similar facilities receive, the Department distributes legislativelydirected supplemental payments to the Maine Veterans' Home. These supplemental payments would be incongruent with this proposal, as the additional funds would be an inappropriate accompaniment to the reimbursement methodology intended to cover 100% of allowable costs and would likely violate Upper Payment Limits established by CMS.
The Department encourages the committee to oppose LD 182 in recognition of recent nursing facility rate reform efforts. Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your
deliberation of this bill.
